bib.title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

question: Can generative trajectory modeling with a causally masked transformer, conditioned on desired return, replace TD-learning based offline RL?
hypothesis: Sequence modeling of (return-to-go, state, action) can perform policy optimisation without dynamic programming, bootstrapping or value pessimism, and help long-term credit assignment.
contributions: Decision Transformer: RL cast as return-conditioned sequence modeling with a GPT
Matches or exceeds model-free offline RL (CQL, BEAR, BRAC, AWR, REM, QR-DQN) on Atari, OpenAI Gym (D4RL) and Key-to-Door
Analyses: percentile BC, return conditioning, context length, credit assignment, sparse rewards

method.summary: A GPT is trained on offline trajectories as interleaved (return-to-go, state, action) tokens, predicting actions (cross-entropy for discrete, MSE for continuous). At test time a target return is given and decremented by observed reward each step; the last K timesteps (3K tokens) are the context.
method.task: offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling

datasets.name: Atari DQN-replay (1%)
datasets.split: 1% of DQN-replay per Agarwal et al.
datasets.preprocessing: scores normalised to gamer=100, random=0 (Hafner et al.)

datasets.name: D4RL Gym locomotion (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker) medium / medium-replay / medium-expert
datasets.size: medium 1 million timesteps; medium-replay approx 25k-400k timesteps; medium-expert 1 million medium + 1 million expert timesteps

datasets.name: Reacher (2D, own generation, not in D4RL)
datasets.source: datasets generated with a methodology similar to D4RL

datasets.name: Graph shortest path random walks
datasets.size: 1,000 random-walk trajectories of T = 10 steps; random graph of 20 nodes, edge sparsity 0.1

models.name: CQL, BEAR, BRAC-v, AWR, REM, QR-DQN

other.source: numbers reported from CQL, REM and D4RL papers; BC run by authors

training.objective: cross-entropy on action (discrete) or MSE (continuous), averaged over timesteps; states and returns not predicted in main experiments
training.optimizer: Atari: Adam betas (0.9, 0.95); Gym: AdamW with PyTorch defaults
training.lr_schedule: Atari: linear warmup and cosine decay; Gym: linear warmup for first 10^5 training steps
training.steps: Gym DT 10^5 gradient steps; Gym BC 2.5x10^4 gradient steps

other.return_to_go_conditioning_atari: 90 Breakout, 2500 Qbert, 20 Pong, 1450 Seaquest (1x or 5x max dataset return)
other.return_to_go_conditioning_gym: 6000 HalfCheetah, 3600 Hopper, 5000 Walker, 50 Reacher (expert; 50% for HalfCheetah)

inference.decoding: autoregressive action prediction; target return decremented by achieved reward
inference.samples: 3 seeds; evaluation episodes per seed not stated
inference.prompting: target return-to-go as first token (desired performance prompt)

metrics.name: normalised episode return
metrics.definition: Atari: 100 = professional gamer, 0 = random; D4RL: 100 = expert

eval.protocol: mean and variance (reported as +-) over 3 seeds; CQL/REM/QR-DQN numbers copied from their papers; BC run by authors

availability.data: public DQN-replay and D4RL; Reacher self-generated

limits: Offline only; online RL benefits are conjecture (Sec 5.8)
Atari uses only 1% of replay data and four games; D4RL only medium-level datasets
%BC optimal percentile needs environment rollouts, so it is an analysis device
Return targets chosen by hand per environment (expert level, 50% for HalfCheetah)
Deterministic returns only; stochastic settings left to future work
Compute, hardware and evaluation episode count not stated
Concedes errors/negative consequences of transformers in MDPs are underexplored
